𝗠𝗲𝗲𝘁 𝗢𝗿𝗹𝘆!

Born and raised in Los Angeles, Orly Cohen came to Ohio for Physician Assistant school, intending to eventually move to warmer weather. However, Hashem had other plans. Thanks to Chabad Young Jewish Professionals in Cincinnati, Orly met lifelong friends and her husband, David. She and David have a one-year-old boy, Eli, who keeps their life fun and exhausting.

Orly always knew she would be a proud member of whatever Jewish community she was involved in. She got her love of hosting from her Brazilian mother, who converted to Judaism because she saw the love and beauty in being Jewish. Orly’s mother has always been known to invite more people than her Shabbat table can hold, but somehow manages to make it look easy.

In high school, Orly was voted most likely to host big Shabbat dinners — a trait she is proud to claim today. She has been very involved in the Chabad YJP community since moving to Cincinnati in 2020. She has served on the Adath Israel Nefesh Board, Moishe House, and as a table host for the Mega Challah Bake.

Orly believes that the best part of being a Jew is having a community of chosen family. She would not have been able to succeed in her professional or personal life without the amazing people she has encountered in the Cincinnati Jewish community. She and David look forward to raising Eli with those same Jewish values.

Israeli born Ifat Lahyani learned from an early age that the heart of a Jewish home is faith, family, hospitality and the warmth of a shared table. These values guide her every day.

Together with her husband, Nadav, and their five children—Noam, Agam, Shoham, Yogev, and Liam—Ifat has created a home where Shabbat and Jewish holidays are celebrated with joy, and where guests are welcomed like family. Throughout the year, she opens her home for Shabbat meals, holiday gatherings, and her annual Mimouna celebration.

One of the defining chapters of Ifat’s life came when she faced cancer. Throughout her journey, faith in Hashem was her greatest source of strength, allowing her to emerge with a renewed sense of purpose, deeper gratitude, and a stronger commitment to a life centered on faith, family and giving to others. Following her recovery, she was blessed with the birth of her youngest son, Liam—a daily reminder that even after life’s greatest challenges, Hashem brings new beginnings and unexpected blessings.

Inspired by that journey, Ifat fulfilled her dream of opening Koriela Kitchen, a kosher bakery and catering company built on Jewish values. Whether baking challah, preparing holiday meals, or catering celebrations, Ifat believes that food has the power to nourish both body and soul, strengthen Jewish identity, and bring people closer together.

Through hospitality and kindness, Ifat hopes to continue inspiring others to celebrate Jewish life, build meaningful connections, and pass these traditions on to future generations.

*Honoree Spotlight*

As we look forward to this year’s Mega Challah Bake, we’re honored to introduce one of the incredible women we’ll be recognizing this year!

Meet Sunny!

Sunny Krantz was raised in Chicago in a family that carried its history quietly. The granddaughter of Holocaust survivors and daughter of a father born in a German refugee camp, she grew up sensing what it means to belong to a people who look after one another. 

Today that inheritance is the center of her life. Sunny has built a majority of her career at the Jewish Federation of Cincinnati, where she leads annual giving and helps sustain Jewish life here and around the world. Ask about her work and she won’t mention the millions raised; she’ll talk about the people who show up for one another.

When she returned to Cincinnati in 2022 after a five-year hiatus, the Jewish community welcomed Sunny and her family back with open arms. Her own Jewish life is now rooted at the Jewish Federation, Wise Temple and the Mayerson JCC, and in the friendships she’s found through Chabad’s Feminine Connection. 

Most Friday afternoons you’ll find Sunny making challah - cheating using a bread machine, and with roughly even odds of undercooked or slightly crispy loaves. 

Above all, Sunny is mom to Henry and Sophia and wife to Landon, and her deepest hope is that her children grow up proud to be Jewish. Judaism is a way of life that sustained Sunny’s family and developed her values. Today it’s the foundation of her family, her community and her purpose.

This week at Hebrew School, we went all the way back to the beginning — Creation!

We discovered what Hashem created on each of the Six Days of Creation, but then went a whole lot deeper:

🌊 Hashem didn’t just create the world once — He is continuously creating it every single moment.

Our younger students brought the Six Days of Creation to life with games and hands-on Creation projects, while our older students explored these big ideas and made their own NeeDoh creations!

We’re BACK at Hebrew School! 🎉📚

What a fantastic first class of the new Hebrew School year!

We kicked off our year by discovering what makes the Torah so special and getting to know its five books, with a special introduction to Bereishis, the first book of the Torah and the focus of our learning this year. ✨

And because learning is always better when you can touch it, experience it (and sometimes eat it! 😉), our students created their own adorable “Torah Is My Guide” mini libraries, complete with all five Chumashim and a special treat connected to each one. 📚🍬

Through games, hands-on activities and lots of discovery, we began exploring an idea we’ll come back to throughout the year:

The Torah isn’t just a book we learn: it’s Hashem’s guide for how we live. 💙

We can’t wait for a year of learning, growing, creating and discovering Bereishis together!

Here’s to an amazing year at Hebrew School! 🌟

Sunday was a truly meaningful day as family and friends gathered to honor the memory of Arthur Lipetz ז"ל.
Following the unveiling of Arthur's headstone, everyone came together at Chabad for a beautiful luncheon, lovingly catered by Maple Café. It was a time to share memories, celebrate Arthur's life, and reflect on the impact he had on so many.
The afternoon continued with the dedication and opening of Arthur's Kitchen, a beautiful new community kitchen that will nourish our community for generations to come. From preparing Kiddushim and holiday meals to hosting challah bakes, cooking classes for children and adults, seniors' lunches, and countless other community programs, this kitchen will be a place where people gather, connect, and create.
Arthur's Kitchen commemorates the extraordinary 65-year friendship between Arthur Lipetz ז"ל and Dr. Baruch Benny. Their friendship, which began when they were university students at UBC and continued until Arthur's last breath, was beautifully captured through the photograph now proudly displayed on the kitchen wall.
May Arthur's memory continue to be a blessing, and may the countless acts of kindness, learning, and community that will take place in Arthur's Kitchen serve as a fitting and lasting tribute to his life.
💙 יהי זכרו ברוך

What makes Shabbat different from every other day? ✨

This week at BC Regional Hebrew School, our students explored Shabbat from every angle!

Our younger class raced through their Daily Schedule Challenge, discovering how our weekdays look different from Shabbat, experienced a model Shabbat meal, and created beautiful faux-leather challah covers to bring home. 🕯️🍞

Our older students dove into the 39 Melachot, learning how the things we refrain from doing on Shabbat connect back to the work done in the Mishkan. Then came the Kiddush Factory! 🍇 They squeezed their own grapes for grape juice and created beautiful Kiddush cups and kits to take home.

And, as always, there was time for davening and Hebrew reading — building the skills and Jewish knowledge our students carry with them week after week. 💙

This week is Shabbat Bereishit, when we return to the opening portion of the Torah: “In the beginning.”

The Rebbe taught that how we approach this Shabbat sets the tone for the entire year.

We’ve prayed, reflected, celebrated and danced. Now we get to bring that energy home. Into our relationships. Into our routines. Into the choices we make when life gets busy again.

Start with something you can carry forward. Light Shabbat candles before sunset. Share a meal. Make time for Torah. Choose one mitzvah to make your own.

A year of meaningful Jewish living begins with the next thing we do.

Shabbat Shalom, Charlotte! Let’s begin with purpose.

This Sukkot, Chabad arranged a special day of visits for children to bring the joy and spirit of the holiday to seniors at the JCC Apartments, The Renoir, and Trinity Lodge.

The children and seniors quickly bonded as they played games, sang together, shook the lulav and etrog and enjoyed special performances by the kids. 🎶🌿

The children also baked delicious oatmeal raisin cookies especially for the seniors, adding a sweet treat to a wonderful afternoon! 🍪

There was so much laughter, singing, smiles, and connection throughout the day. 😊❤️

It was truly an amazing and uplifting experience, as the children brought happiness, warmth, and the joy of Sukkot to so many wonderful seniors in our community.

items.caption:
Sunday Morning BLT = Bagels, Lox, and Tefillin!
This week, we marked the end of the Shloshim, the 30 day mourning period, for the victims of the Bondi Beach Massacre, who were attacked celebrating Chanukah at Chabad of Bondi Beach.

Just minutes before the attack, the Chabad Rabbi in Bondi Beach, Rabbi Eli Schlanger, was helping others put on Tefillin - a daily Mitzvah for Jewish Men that brings holiness to our minds and hearts.

In his memory, Chabad of Winnipeg is launching a weekly open house with bagels, lox, tefillin, and lots of Jewish energy!

Drop by this Sunday at 9:30 AM at Chabad’s Ahava Halpern Building, 1845 Mathers Ave. to start off your week right!

latestPosts.caption:
We celebrated my 36th Birthday one day early! My incredible wife Alicia planned an incredible day and I had no idea what she had in store. 

1. Quick stop in San Jose to get breakfast pastries from a fun bakery. The Ube cheesecake was insane!

2. Then we went to Goodwill to pick put weird outfits for whatever she had planned later. BONUS we found an epic wolf snowboard jacket as an extra bday gift. Then we went to an Asian supermarket to snag delicious snacks and drinks and relax at a park while Alicia was making something out of a huge roll of yarn.

3. Then off to a great sushi lunch before making our way to San Francisco! Where we got dressed up and she reveals two tiny Big Wheels in the trunk for a crazy downhill bigwheel race down one of the steepest and curviest streets in San Francisco! The yarn was to add some silly pant strings to my already wacky outfit. We climbed up the hill through huge crowds of racers and spectators and joined the starting crowd. I was waaaayyy to big for my tricycle which added to the fun. Started at a slow start trying to scoot to the slope but then quickly picked up speed as we drifted around corners and crashed into other riders on the way down. It was insane and super fun! Somehow neither of us got hurt! Felt like Live Action Mario Kart!

4. We went to Chinatown and grabbed some boba tea and a giant cookie as we explored and took fun pics.

5. Dinner was dim sum with some delicious buns and noodles before a quick foot massage at a Chinese masseuse. Then on the final event which was a crazy fun and impressive big gay circus! The performance was amazing and hilarious.

Incredible day from start to finish!

My wife @theladylaufer is amazing!
